# .github/workflows
- `staging.yml` — **`develop`’s deploy target.** Every push to `develop` applies the migrations to `memento-mori-staging` and deploys `memento-mori-staging` — so a change can be checked from a phone before the release PR is merged. A **separate file from `ci.yml` on purpose**: the two need opposite concurrency policies, because CI cancels a superseded run and a deploy must never be cancelled between "migrations applied" and "Worker deployed". It does not run the tests (`ci.yml` does, on the same push) and does not `npm ci` (only wrangler runs). **Seeding is `npm run seed:staging` or `workflow_dispatch` + `reseed`, never automatic** — seeding on every push would wipe whatever you were half way through testing. **`workflow_dispatch` needs the workflow file on the DEFAULT branch**, so the Run-workflow button does not exist until a release carries `staging.yml` into `main`; `npm run seed:staging` is the path that always works.
- `ci.yml` — **The gate before develop.** `npm test` on every pull request and every push to `develop`. It exists because `npm test` otherwise ran only in the local push hook — which a cloud session's PR and a browser merge both miss — and in the release job, by which point the code is already on `main`. Deliberately ONE job: `test-api.js` already applies every migration and `worker/seed.sql` to a real SQLite database, so a `wrangler d1 migrations apply --local` step would download wrangler to re-prove that. `test` is the required check on `main`.
- `release.yml` — the only path to live; CLAUDE.md "Git workflow" has the order. Needs the repo secrets `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`.
